extracted.intended_audience: scholarly publishers, journal editors, editorial teams, and publishing professionals
extracted.subtask_short: reducing reviewer fatigue in scholarly journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for scholarly publishers and editorial teams on diagnosing reviewer fatigue and implementing policies, processes, incentives, and AI tools to reduce reviewer burden and improve peer review quality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Volume of Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The global increase in research output has led to a surge in manuscript submissions, placing a heavier burden on reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat high submission volume as a root cause of reviewer fatigue; consider intake controls, triage, and automation to reduce the number of full peer reviews required. Monitor submission trends and match reviewer capacity to submission load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Academics often juggle multiple professional responsibilities, leaving little time for thorough reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge reviewers' competing commitments when setting deadlines and workloads. Use streamlined review forms and automated assistance to reduce time per review, and offer flexible timelines or extensions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewing is generally a voluntary activity with limited direct rewards or recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement tangible and recognition-based incentives (certificates, discounts, access, public acknowledgement) to increase willingness to review and sustain reviewer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated Requests to a Small Pool
rubrics_metrics.description: A small pool of expert reviewers is frequently called upon, exacerbating reviewer burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track reviewer load and limit repeat requests. Broaden the reviewer pool (see 'Broadening the Reviewer Pool') and implement rotation systems to distribute requests more evenly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity of Research
rubrics_metrics.description: The increasing specialization and complexity of research make reviews more time-consuming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match manuscripts to reviewers with appropriate expertise and provide targeted review guidance; consider splitting technical checks (e.g., stats/integrity) to specialist reviewers or AI-assisted checks to reduce time burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decreased Review Quality (Consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overburdened reviewers may provide rushed or superficial assessments, compromising the quality of the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor review quality signals (length, depth, number of comments). Use training, clearer review forms, and AI assistance to support deeper, higher-quality reviews rather than rushing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed Publication Timelines (Consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortage of willing reviewers leads to longer review cycles, delaying the dissemination of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address bottlenecks through reviewer recruitment, automated triage, AI summaries, and flexible deadlines to accelerate decision-making without degrading review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Reviewer Pool (Consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: As fatigue grows, fewer scholars are willing to engage in peer review, creating a vicious cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in incentives, recognition, training for early-career reviewers, and broaden reviewer demographics to expand and sustain the pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damage to Academic Reputation (Consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The credibility of the peer review system is jeopardized, potentially diminishing trust in published research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize measures that protect review robustness (integrity checks, quality controls, transparent processes) and communicate these safeguards to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and Incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer tangible rewards (certificates, discounts on publication fees, or access to journal content) and public recognition (acknowledgements in the journal or on its website).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a mix of material and reputational incentives tailored to reviewer motivations; advertise these benefits when inviting reviewers and track uptake to evaluate effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined Review Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement efficient manuscript management systems and clear, concise review forms to simplify the review process and reduce administrative burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt manuscript systems that minimize administrative tasks for reviewers, redesign review forms to focus on essential evaluative questions, and remove unnecessary steps that prolong reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Training and Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer training programs and provide access to guidelines and other helpful materials to help reviewers understand expectations and conduct high-quality reviews efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide onboarding, exemplar reviews, checklists, and short training modules, especially targeted at early-career reviewers; measure whether training improves review thoroughness and speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening the Reviewer Pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively recruit new reviewers, including early-career researchers, and diversify the pool by including international reviewers and those from underrepresented disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted recruitment, mentorship, and development pathways to integrate new reviewers; track diversity metrics and workload distribution to ensure broadened participation reduces pressure on core reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow more flexible timelines for completing reviews and provide extensions when needed, recognizing reviewers have other commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt flexible policies (reasonable default deadlines, easy extension requests) to reduce stress and improve completion rates; balance flexibility with editorial timelines and communicate expectations clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Review Load
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the number of manuscripts a reviewer is asked to review within a certain timeframe and implement a rotation system to distribute workload more evenly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set caps on review invitations per reviewer over set periods and use rotation schemes to prevent over-reliance on individuals. Monitor compliance and adjust invitations based on recent commitments and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Tools for Initial Screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI and machine learning tools to assist with initial manuscript screening and identify potential reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement automated triage to filter out unsuitable submissions early, reducing the number of full peer reviews required; use ML to match reviewer expertise and availability, but retain human oversight for borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and Formatting Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement tools to check for plagiarism or basic formatting issues, reducing the burden on human reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run automated checks for plagiarism, reference formatting, and basic compliance before sending to peer review so reviewers focus on substantive critique rather than mechanical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Support Structures (Mentorship and Peer Networks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer mentorship programs and create peer support networks to provide training and opportunities for reviewers to connect and share experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up mentor–mentee review pairings, peer discussion forums, and community resources to help new reviewers learn efficient practices and reduce isolation that can contribute to burnout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Review Summarization
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can generate concise summaries of peer review reports, providing a clear and efficient overview of key feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI summaries to help editors and authors quickly understand major points from multiple reviews; ensure summaries are verified by humans and used as an aid rather than a replacement for full reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Based Translation for Accessibility and Inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-powered translation tools support non-native English-speaking reviewers and authors by translating manuscripts and reviews with high accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt translation tools to widen reviewer participation and improve inclusivity, but review translated content for nuance and accuracy in technical language.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Based Fact-Checking for Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools assist reviewers by automatically verifying facts, data, and references in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy automated fact-checking to reduce cognitive load on reviewers; ensure systems flag items for human verification and that false positives/negatives are managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Matching Optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: AI optimizes assignment of manuscripts to reviewers by analyzing reviewer profiles, expertise, and workloads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data-driven matching to improve fit between manuscript content and reviewer expertise while considering recent workload to avoid overburdening individuals; periodically audit matching algorithms for bias and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Powered Peer Review Reports (AI Agents)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated peer review reports provide an additional layer of analysis and insight, helping to identify potential issues that may have been overlooked by human reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ AI agents to produce preliminary or complementary review reports that highlight methodological concerns, inconsistencies, or potential misconduct; ensure these reports are used to augment human judgment and are transparent to editors/authors regarding AI involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed and Efficiency via AI
rubrics_metrics.description: AI agents can process and analyze manuscripts rapidly, generating preliminary review reports in a fraction of the time it takes human reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage AI to shorten time-to-decision, especially for high-volume journals; maintain quality checks so speed gains do not degrade substantive evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and Objectivity from AI
rubrics_metrics.description: AI agents provide consistent and objective evaluations based on predefined criteria, ensuring that all manuscripts are assessed against the same standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI to reduce variability across reviews on routine criteria, but monitor for systematic biases in training data and ensure human oversight for subjective judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying Key Areas of Focus
rubrics_metrics.description: AI agents can highlight specific areas of a manuscript that may require closer scrutiny by human reviewers, such as statistical analysis or data integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI to triage and flag technical or high-risk sections for expert human review, enabling more efficient allocation of reviewer effort to the most consequential issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augmenting Reviewer Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated reports can provide additional insights, especially in areas where human reviewers may lack specific expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement human reviewers with AI-provided checks (statistical, methodological, reference consistency) while ensuring final judgments remain with qualified humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing Reviewer Fatigue via Task Automation
rubrics_metrics.description: By handling routine or technical aspects of the review process, AI agents alleviate the burden on human reviewers, allowing them to focus on nuanced elements of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automate repetitive tasks (format checks, reference verification, basic reproducibility checks) to free reviewer time for substantive critique; evaluate automation impact on reviewer satisfaction and review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Driven Editorial Support (Platforms like Author Pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms provide advanced language and technical assessments, generate quality reports, and automate manuscript triage to support editorial teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt editorial AI platforms to assist editorial decision-making and pre-review processing, ensuring integration with human workflows and transparent reporting of AI outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Editing (Tools like Wyse)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-powered editing tools ensure manuscripts are clear, accurate, and adhere to editorial standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automated editing to reduce the editorial and reviewer burden of correcting language and presentation issues before peer review; keep human copyediting for nuance and final quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-Driven Reviewer Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: AI optimizes reviewer matching by analyzing expertise, past performance, and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytics to recommend reviewers with appropriate subject matter expertise and current availability; incorporate past review quality metrics while guarding against reinforcing exclusionary patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Integrity Checks
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools detect academic misconduct by analyzing textual similarities, citation patterns, and other indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate integrity checks (plagiarism, citation anomalies, image manipulation detectors) into editorial workflows prior to peer review to reduce wasted reviewer effort and protect research quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced Human-AI Integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine AI-generated reports with traditional human reviews to leverage speed, objectivity, and data processing while preserving human expertise and judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a hybrid model where AI handles routine, technical, and triage tasks and humans retain final evaluative authority; ensure transparency about AI's role, monitor outcomes, and iterate policies to preserve fairness and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI to Enhance Reviewer Well-Being
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of AI tools has the potential to significantly improve reviewer well-being by automating routine tasks, enhancing accuracy, and optimizing workload distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reviewer satisfaction and well-being before and after AI deployment; prioritize tools that demonstrably reduce time burden and cognitive load without compromising review quality or introducing bias.
